import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Set the style of seaborn

# Create a boxplot to visualize the distribution of transaction amounts by fraud status
sns.boxplot(x='is_fraud', y='amount', data=data, palette='Set2')

# Add titles and labels

plt.xlabel('Fraud Status (0 = No Fraud, 1 = Fraud)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a boxplot to visualize the distribution of transaction amounts by fraud status
sns.boxplot(x='is_fraud', y='amount', data=data, palette='Set2')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amounts by Fraud Status', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Fraud Status (0 = No Fraud, 1 = Fraud)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
